d1.purpose: Help diners choose a dinner dish with an understanding of its ingredients, price and allergens.
tasks: Scan dishes within Starters, Mains and Desserts to find appealing options.
Read a dish name together with its description to understand what is served.
Compare prices across dishes and locate allergen information before ordering.
relations: Each dish name, description, price and allergen entry belongs to one row.
Section labels group dishes by course and span the whole table.
Prices and allergens qualify individual dishes rather than the course as a whole.
roles: Dish names are row headers and the main anchors for scanning.
Descriptions provide the longest continuous prose.
Prices are short values intended for quick comparison.
Allergen entries support lookup and may contain several items.
Column headers identify the information in each column; course rows divide the menu into sections.
keep_whole: Allergen names and other unbreakable terms.
Dish names where practical, especially when scanning the menu.
may_wrap: Multiword dish names and allergen lists when needed, without splitting individual words.
same_scale: Dish names should have a consistent column width across courses.
Descriptions and allergen entries should each retain consistent widths across all dishes.
Course labels share the full table width and the same structural role.
d1.h_vs_v: The 720px limit requires prose to wrap. More description width reduces row height and supports continuous reading, while more dish or allergen width improves scanning and lookup; the compact price column needs little space.

d2.purpose: Present a dinner menu that helps diners choose dishes within each course.
tasks: Scan starters, mains and desserts for appealing dishes.
Read descriptions to understand ingredients and preparation.
Compare prices and check allergens before choosing.
relations: Each dish name, description, price and allergen entry belongs to the same row.
Each full-width course label groups the dishes below it.
roles: Dish names are row headers and the primary anchors for scanning.
Descriptions provide the most detailed reading material.
Prices support quick comparison and need little horizontal space.
Allergen entries support safety checks and must remain easy to associate with their dishes.
Course labels divide the menu into sections.
same_scale: Dish names share one column and a consistent hierarchy.
Descriptions share one column; prices and allergen entries each share their own comparison axis.
Course labels have the same full-width structural role.
d2.h_vs_v: The 720px viewport requires descriptions or allergen lists to wrap. More width for one reduces wrapping there but increases row height elsewhere; enough width for dish names helps preserve the scanning anchors.

d3.purpose: Present a dinner menu that helps diners choose dishes with awareness of ingredients, prices and allergens.
tasks: Find each dish's price and allergen information.
relations: Each dish, description, price and allergen entry belongs to the same row.
Course headings group the dishes that follow them.
roles: Dish names are row headers and primary lookup anchors.
Prices are compact values for comparison.
Allergen entries provide dish-specific dietary information.
Starters, Mains and Desserts are full-width group headings.
keep_whole: Price values and their currency symbols.
may_wrap: Multiword dish names and allergen lists when needed.
same_scale: Dish rows should have a consistent hierarchy across courses.
Course headings should share the same full-width treatment.
Prices should occupy a consistent, compact column.
d3.h_vs_v: Description prose can absorb several lines, while dish names, prices and allergens benefit from enough width for quick scanning. Allocating more width to descriptions reduces row height; allocating more to allergens or dish names improves those lookup paths but makes descriptions taller.

analysis.strengths: All text is visible, headers stay on one line, and no words break internally. Every dish row is two lines tall, giving the menu a steady rhythm. The dessert allergens fit in two lines, with “Tree nuts (hazelnut)” kept together.
analysis.faults: Four of the five dish names wrap, making the first column slower to scan. “Gluten (wheat)” is split across lines in the croquettes row.
analysis.spatial_logic: P gives most space to descriptions and a comparatively generous share to allergens, accepting wrapped dish names to keep every row within two lines.

analysis.strengths: Every dish name is on one line, making the first column easy to scan. Descriptions remain at two lines, and “Gluten (wheat)” stays together. All text fits without internal word breaks.
analysis.faults: The dessert allergen list takes three lines and separates “Tree nuts” from “(hazelnut)”. This makes the final row taller and leaves more empty space beside it.
analysis.spatial_logic: Q gives dish names enough width to stay whole, taking most of that space from allergens. Its slightly wider description column does not reduce the number of lines in the rendered descriptions.

analysis.strengths: Like Q, R keeps every dish name on one line, keeps descriptions to two lines, and preserves “Gluten (wheat)” as a unit. All text is visible without internal word breaks.
analysis.faults: The dessert allergen list still takes three lines and separates “Tree nuts” from “(hazelnut)”, producing the same taller final row as Q. Its small shift of space to allergens does not visibly improve the wrapping.
analysis.spatial_logic: R retains Q’s wide dish column but transfers four pixels from description to allergens. In the shown rendering, that adjustment does not cross a useful line-break threshold.

rounds.insights: The key trade-off is between one-line dish names and coherent, compact allergen lists. P makes the better overall use of space among the shown layouts: its wrapped names remain readable, while the dessert allergen stays grouped and all item rows share the same height. Q and R improve name scanning but give up that grouping without gaining shorter descriptions. Small width changes matter only when they cross an actual wrapping threshold, so proposed alternatives need rendered verification.

analysis.strengths: All headers and prices fit on one line, descriptions read in two lines, and no words are broken.
analysis.faults: The dessert allergen list takes three lines, isolating “(hazelnut)” on the last line. The croquettes allergen list also separates “(wheat)” from “Gluten.”
analysis.spatial_logic: The generous description column supports continuous reading, but the allergen column is just too narrow for the longest list, making the dessert row taller than the other dish rows.

analysis.strengths: The wider allergen column keeps the dessert list to two lines and retains “Tree nuts (hazelnut)” together.
analysis.faults: The narrower description column leaves “aioli” and “jus” on third lines in two rows. “(wheat)” remains separated from “Gluten.”
analysis.spatial_logic: Width shifts from descriptions to allergens, improving the dessert row at the expense of two prominent descriptions and producing uneven row heights.

analysis.strengths: The chicken description fits in two lines, and the headers and prices remain clear.
analysis.faults: The croquettes description leaves “aioli” alone on a third line, while the dessert allergen list isolates “(hazelnut)” on a third line.
analysis.spatial_logic: Extra width in the dish column does not prevent the two main dish names from wrapping, while the description and allergen columns each incur a three-line cell.

analysis.strengths: Every dish row is two lines tall, all headers and prices fit, and the dessert allergen list keeps “Tree nuts (hazelnut)” together. Descriptions have natural breaks without isolated final words.
analysis.faults: Four dish names wrap, and the croquettes allergen list separates “(wheat)” from “Gluten.”
analysis.spatial_logic: A narrower dish column gives descriptions and allergens enough room for a consistent two-line rhythm. The wrapped dish names remain easy to scan alongside their descriptions and prices.

rounds.insights: The useful width thresholds differ by column: a small increase in allergen width keeps the dessert list to two lines, while the descriptions need enough space to avoid isolated third-line words. Narrowing the dish column in P accepts readable name wraps and gives the longer content a more even rhythm.

contrast.why: Equal widths waste space on the short prices and leave the descriptions and allergen lists unnecessarily narrow. The resulting extra wrapping would make the menu harder to scan and much taller.

synthesis.rationale: Layout P gives descriptions and allergens enough room for all entries to fit within two lines, with an even rhythm across the dish rows. Layout Q is a distinct, comparable choice: all dish names stay on one line, making them easier to scan, though the dessert allergen list takes three lines. Both fit the viewport and preserve whole words.

general: Allocate width according to content and reading task, rather than making columns equal by default.
Keep related terms together where practical, especially when line breaks affect lookup or interpretation.
Judge row height alongside the quality of the breaks that produce it.
specific: The price column needs little width because both its header and values are short.
Extra width for dish names can put every name on one line, but reduces space available for the longer allergen lists.

synthesis.tradeoffs: P wraps four dish names but keeps each allergen list to two lines or fewer. Q keeps every dish name on one line and keeps 'Gluten (wheat)' together, but separates 'Tree nuts' from '(hazelnut)' and gives the dessert row a third line. R makes essentially the same tradeoff as Q; s0A also separates the nut qualifier, while s0B and s0C leave 'aioli' alone on a line.
synthesis.uncertain: The preferred finalist depends on whether readers place more value on scanning complete dish names or reading compact allergen lists. No user testing is provided.
